title: Races, deadlocks, and visibility
hook: A race is two threads interleaving a multi-step invariant. A deadlock is waits that cycle. Visibility is the third bug: a write that never becomes visible because the memory model allowed it to stay local.

sections.heading: Races are about invariants, not ‘two threads exist’
sections.prose: check-then-act on a Dictionary without a lock is a race: both threads see missing key, both insert. ++ on int is a race. Even bool flags can tear in interesting ways without barriers. The C# memory model allows compilers and CPUs to reorder ordinary reads and writes. A lock (or Interlocked, or volatile in its narrow sense) introduces acquire/release semantics so that writes inside a locked region become visible to the next thread that takes the same lock. If only one method takes the lock, you have a race with the unlocked reader. Deadlocks: thread A holds lock1 waits lock2; B the reverse. Also: thread holds a lock and waits for a Task whose continuation needs the same lock or the same SynchronizationContext. Also: two RabbitMQ consumers waiting on each other’s in-memory gate. Fix with lock ordering, smaller sections, and never waiting for I/O or another lock while holding one.

snippets.label: Lock ordering and no I/O under the lock
snippets.explanation: A consistent order avoids the classic two-lock deadlock. The section still must not call Redis.

sections.heading: Visibility without a data race in the language sense
sections.prose: You can write a field from one thread and read it from another with no crash and still see a stale value forever if the JIT hoists the read in a loop. That is the _shouldStop example. lock or Interlocked.CompareExchange publishes. Double-checked locking for a singleton requires a volatile field or Lazy<T> because the first read of the instance must see all writes that constructed it. Prefer Lazy<T> or static initialization. Interviewers who ask about the .NET memory model want: locks hide reordering; Interlocked is a full fence for that location; do not invent your own lock-free queue unless you can name acquire and release.

interviewTakeaways: Protect the whole invariant with the same lock object.
Deadlock: lock order, or waiting (including await/Result) while holding a lock.
Publication of constructed objects: Lazy<T> or lock, not a naked static bool.
commonPitfalls: lock on string keys that intern.
Waiting on a Task inside a lock that the continuation also needs.

jsTsCorrelations.concept: Single-threaded races still exist via interleaving awaits
jsTsCorrelations.note: JS has no data race on small fields between workers unless SharedArrayBuffer is used, but await interleaving still breaks check-then-act on a Map. C# adds true parallel races plus visibility.
